name: What to Expect During a Multi-Story Addition

step.name: Step 1: Existing Structure Investigation & Planning (1-3 Months): This init…
step.text: Existing Structure Investigation & Planning (1-3 Months): This initial phase is all about understanding your home's bones. An existing-structure investigation will determine if your foundation and walls can handle the extra load. Simultaneously, we'll review zoning and height limits and begin architectural planning, including how new stairs, circulation, and utilities will integrate. LineWork Development's architectural background helps us ensure the design is both functional and buildable, anticipating challenges early.

step.name: Step 2: Structural Engineering & Detailed Design (Ongoing with Planning): O…
step.text: Structural Engineering & Detailed Design (Ongoing with Planning): Once the conceptual plan is in place, structural engineers will get involved. They'll analyze your home's foundation and supporting walls, then design new framing, account for lateral loads (like wind or seismic forces), and plan for temporary shoring. This is when detailed building, electrical, plumbing, and mechanical plans are developed to ensure everything works together seamlessly.

step.name: Step 3: Permit Review & Approval (3 Weeks-3 Months+): With all plans finali…
step.text: Permit Review & Approval (3 Weeks-3 Months+): With all plans finalized and engineered, they'll be submitted to your local jurisdiction for permit review. This phase can vary widely in duration. Incomplete applications or zoning conflicts can extend this significantly, highlighting the importance of thorough initial planning. LineWork Development handles the permit navigation, streamlining this often complex step.

step.name: Step 4: Construction & Framing (8-12 Weeks+ for Structural): Once permits a…
step.text: Construction & Framing (8-12 Weeks+ for Structural): Once permits are in hand, construction begins. This includes site preparation, temporary weather protection, and the significant work of building the new structural frame. This phase is often the most disruptive, especially if you're living in the home, due to the need for shoring and opening up the roof and walls.

step.name: Step 5: Enclosure, Systems & Finishes (Varies): After the new story is fram…
step.text: Enclosure, Systems & Finishes (Varies): After the new story is framed and weatherproofed, electrical, plumbing, and HVAC systems are installed. This is followed by insulation, drywall, and finally, interior and exterior finishes. Throughout this period, staged inspections will occur to ensure everything meets code.

step.name: Step 6: Final Inspections & Walkthrough: The project culminates with final…
step.text: Final Inspections & Walkthrough: The project culminates with final inspections and a walkthrough to address any punch-list items, ensuring everything is to your satisfaction and ready for you to enjoy. Our transparent communication and organized project control, utilizing digital tools, keep you informed of progress, budgets, and schedules throughout.
